lessons.title: Say what you have (never) done
lessons.summary: Talk about your experiences, and ask about other people's: “Have you ever climbed Mt Fuji?” “No, never.”
lessons.topic: plain past + {{ことがあります|koto ga arimasu}}; {{一度も|ichido mo}} + negative

goal.t: 富士山に登ったことがありますか。
goal.r: Fujisan ni nobotta koto ga arimasu ka.
goal.tr: Have you ever climbed Mt Fuji?

dialog.t: 納豆を食べたことがありますか。
dialog.r: Nattō o tabeta koto ga arimasu ka.
dialog.tr: Have you ever eaten natto?

dialog.t: はい、一度あります。
dialog.r: Hai, ichido arimasu.
dialog.tr: Yes, once.

dialog.t: どうでしたか。
dialog.r: Dō deshita ka.
dialog.tr: How was it?

dialog.t: ちょっと苦手でした。ゆいさんは外国に行ったことがありますか。
dialog.r: Chotto nigate deshita. Yui-san wa gaikoku ni itta koto ga arimasu ka.
dialog.tr: Not really my thing. Have you ever been abroad, Yui?

dialog.t: いいえ、一度もありません。でも、いつかイギリスへ行きたいです。
dialog.r: Iie, ichido mo arimasen. Demo, itsuka Igirisu e ikitai desu.
dialog.tr: No, never. But I'd like to go to Britain someday.

blocks.p: **Have you ever…?: plain past + {{ことがあります|koto ga arimasu}}.** Word for word “there is the fact that I did…”: {{富士山に登ったことがあります|Fujisan ni nobotta koto ga arimasu}} “I've climbed Mt Fuji (at some point)”. The verb before {{こと|koto}} is always in the plain past, the ta-form.

**Never.** {{ことがありません|koto ga arimasen}} “I've never…”. {{一度も|ichido mo}} “not even once” makes it stronger: {{一度も行ったことがありません|ichido mo itta koto ga arimasen}}. Short answers use just {{あります|arimasu}}: {{はい、あります|hai, arimasu}}, {{いいえ、ありません|iie, arimasen}}. How many times: {{一度|ichido}} or {{一回|ikkai}} “once”, {{二回|ni-kai}} “twice”.

**An experience, not one event.** {{昨日、すしを食べました|kinō, sushi o tabemashita}} says what you did yesterday. {{すしを食べたことがあります|sushi o tabeta koto ga arimasu}} says that sushi is part of your experience. So {{ことがある|koto ga aru}} never goes with a time like {{昨日|kinō}}.

table: {{日本へ行ったことがあります。|Nihon e itta koto ga arimasu.}}
{{日本へ行ったことがありません。|Nihon e itta koto ga arimasen.}}
{{日本へ行ったことがありますか。|Nihon e itta koto ga arimasu ka.}}
Have you ever been to Japan?
{{去年、日本へ行きました。|Kyonen, Nihon e ikimashita.}}
I went to Japan last year.

ex.t: 着物を着たことがあります。
ex.r: Kimono o kita koto ga arimasu.
ex.tr: I've worn a kimono.

ex.t: 一度も海外へ行ったことがありません。
ex.r: Ichido mo kaigai e itta koto ga arimasen.
ex.tr: I've never been abroad.

ex.t: 日本の映画を見たことがありますか。
ex.r: Nihon no eiga o mita koto ga arimasu ka.
ex.tr: Have you ever seen a Japanese movie?

ex.tr: I've been to Okinawa twice.

ex.t: 有名な人に会ったことがありますか。
ex.r: Yūmei na hito ni atta koto ga arimasu ka.
ex.tr: Have you ever met a famous person?

ex.t: はい、一度あります。
ex.r: Hai, ichido arimasu.
ex.tr: Yes, once.

blocks.tip: {{会います|aimasu}} “meet” takes {{に|ni}} for the person: {{田中さんに会いました|Tanaka-san ni aimashita}} “I met Mr Tanaka”.

mistakes.wrong: 日本へ行くことがあります。

mistakes.why: For experiences, the verb before {{こと|koto}} is in the plain past. ({{行くことがあります|iku koto ga arimasu}} means “I sometimes go”.)

mistakes.right: 昨日、すしを食べました。
mistakes.rw: Kinō, sushi o tabeta koto ga arimasu.
mistakes.why: {{ことがある|koto ga aru}} is for experience in general; with a time like {{昨日|kinō}}, use the ordinary past.

lessons.title: Give examples of what you do
lessons.summary: Mention a few things you do, without listing everything: “At weekends I watch movies, go shopping, that kind of thing.”
lessons.topic: {{～たり、～たりします|… tari, … tari shimasu}}

goal.t: 週末は映画を見たり、買い物をしたりします。
goal.r: Shūmatsu wa eiga o mitari, kaimono o shitari shimasu.
goal.tr: At weekends I watch movies, go shopping and so on.

dialog.t: 休みの日は何をしていますか。
dialog.r: Yasumi no hi wa nani o shite imasu ka.
dialog.tr: What do you do on your days off?

dialog.t: 家で本を読んだり、友達と食事をしたりします。
dialog.r: Ie de hon o yondari, tomodachi to shokuji o shitari shimasu.
dialog.tr: I read at home, eat out with friends, things like that.

dialog.t: そうですか。旅行は？
dialog.r: Sō desu ka. Ryokō wa?
dialog.tr: I see. What about travelling?

dialog.t: 時々します。去年の夏は、京都でお寺を見たり、着物を着たりしました。
dialog.r: Tokidoki shimasu. Kyonen no natsu wa, Kyōto de otera o mitari, kimono o kitari shimashita.
dialog.tr: Sometimes. Last summer I visited temples in Kyoto, wore a kimono and so on.

blocks.p: **A few examples: {{～たり、～たりします|… tari, … tari shimasu}}.** Take the plain past (ta-form), add {{り|ri}}, list two or three actions, and finish with {{します|shimasu}}: {{見たり、買い物をしたりします|mitari, kaimono o shitari shimasu}} “I watch movies, go shopping and so on”. It tells the listener these are examples, not the full list. The tense goes on the final {{します|shimasu}}: {{…したりしました|… shitari shimashita}} “I did things like…”.

**Back and forth.** With opposite actions, it means “now this, now that”: {{行ったり来たりしています|ittari kitari shite imasu}} “going back and forth”, {{雨が降ったり止んだりしています|ame ga futtari yandari shite imasu}} “it keeps raining on and off”.

Compare the て-form: {{見て、買い物をして、帰りました|mite, kaimono o shite, kaerimashita}} tells everything you did, in order. {{見たり、買い物をしたりしました|mitari, kaimono o shitari shimashita}} gives a sample, in no particular order.

ex.t: 夏休みは泳いだり、山に登ったりしました。
ex.r: Natsuyasumi wa oyoidari, yama ni nobottari shimashita.
ex.tr: In the summer holidays I swam, climbed mountains and so on.

ex.t: 日曜日は掃除をしたり、洗濯をしたりします。
ex.r: Nichiyōbi wa sōji o shitari, sentaku o shitari shimasu.
ex.tr: On Sundays I do the cleaning, the laundry, that kind of thing.

ex.t: パーティーでは歌ったり、踊ったりしました。
ex.r: Pātī de wa utattari, odottari shimashita.
ex.tr: At the party we sang, danced and so on.

ex.t: 雨が降ったり止んだりしています。
ex.r: Ame ga futtari yandari shite imasu.
ex.tr: It keeps raining on and off.

ex.t: 図書館では勉強したり、本を借りたりすることができます。
ex.r: Toshokan de wa benkyō shitari, hon o karitari suru koto ga dekimasu.
ex.tr: At the library you can study, borrow books and so on.

ex.t: 週末は映画を見たりします。
ex.r: Shūmatsu wa eiga o mitari shimasu.
ex.tr: At weekends I watch movies and stuff.
ex.note: one {{たり|tari}} alone: soft and vague

blocks.tip: This is the natural answer to {{休みの日は何をしていますか|yasumi no hi wa nani o shite imasu ka}} “What do you do on your days off?”: it sounds relaxed, not like a timetable.

mistakes.wrong: 映画を見たり、買い物をします。
mistakes.right: 映画を見たり、買い物をしたりします。
mistakes.rw: Eiga o mitari, kaimono o shimasu.
mistakes.rr: Eiga o mitari, kaimono o shitari shimasu.
mistakes.tr: I watch movies, go shopping and so on.
mistakes.why: Each action takes {{たり|tari}}, and {{します|shimasu}} comes at the end.

mistakes.wrong: 泳ぎたり、山に登ったりしました。
mistakes.right: 泳いだり、山に登ったりしました。
mistakes.tr: I swam, climbed mountains and so on.
mistakes.why: {{たり|tari}} is made from the ta-form: {{泳いだ|oyoida}} → {{泳いだり|oyoidari}}.

lessons.title: Compare things and pick the best
lessons.summary: Compare two things, ask which is better, and say what's best of all: “Tokyo is bigger than Osaka.” “Which do you prefer?”
lessons.topic: {{AはBより|A wa B yori}}; {{どちら|dochira}} and {{～のほうが|… no hō ga}}; {{～の中で～が一番|… no naka de … ga ichiban}}

goal.t: 東京は大阪より大きいです。
goal.r: Tōkyō wa Ōsaka yori ōkii desu.
goal.tr: Tokyo is bigger than Osaka.

dialog.t: このシャツとあのシャツ、どちらがいいと思いますか。
dialog.r: Kono shatsu to ano shatsu, dochira ga ii to omoimasu ka.
dialog.tr: This shirt or that one: which do you think is better?

dialog.t: あのシャツのほうがいいと思います。色がきれいです。
dialog.r: Ano shatsu no hō ga ii to omoimasu. Iro ga kirei desu.
dialog.tr: I think that one's better. The colour is lovely.

dialog.t: でも、あのシャツはこのシャツより高いですよ。
dialog.r: Demo, ano shatsu wa kono shatsu yori takai desu yo.
dialog.tr: But that shirt is more expensive than this one.

dialog.t: じゃ、両方買いましょう！
dialog.r: Ja, ryōhō kaimashō!
dialog.tr: Then let's buy both!

blocks.p: **A is more … than B: {{AはBより～|A wa B yori …}}.** {{より|yori}} means “than”, and the adjective doesn't change at all: {{東京は大阪より大きいです|Tōkyō wa Ōsaka yori ōkii desu}} “Tokyo is bigger than Osaka”, word for word “Tokyo, than Osaka, is big”. There's no “-er” or “more”.

**Which of the two?: {{AとB、どちらが～ですか|A to B, dochira ga … desu ka}}.** {{どちら|dochira}} (casually {{どっち|dotchi}}) is “which of the two”. Answer with {{～のほうが|… no hō ga}}, “the side of…”: {{犬のほうが好きです|inu no hō ga suki desu}} “I prefer dogs”. A question word takes {{が|ga}}, and so does the answer.

**The most: {{～の中で～が一番|… no naka de … ga ichiban}}.** {{一番|ichiban}} “number one” before an adjective makes “the most”: {{日本の中で富士山が一番高いです|Nihon no naka de Fujisan ga ichiban takai desu}} “Mt Fuji is the highest in Japan”. Asking: {{何が一番好きですか|nani ga ichiban suki desu ka}} “What do you like best?”. For three or more, “which” is {{どれ|dore}}.

table: {{夏は冬より好きです。|Natsu wa fuyu yori suki desu.}}
I like summer more than winter.
{{夏と冬、どちらが好きですか。|Natsu to fuyu, dochira ga suki desu ka.}}
Which do you like better, summer or winter?
{{夏のほうが好きです。|Natsu no hō ga suki desu.}}
{{一年の中で夏が一番好きです。|Ichinen no naka de natsu ga ichiban suki desu.}}
Summer is my favourite time of year.

lessons.title: Say how things change, and choose
lessons.summary: Talk about change, and say what you've decided on: “It's got cold, hasn't it?” “I'll have the coffee.”
lessons.topic: {{～くなります|… ku narimasu}} and {{～になります|… ni narimasu}}; {{～にします|… ni shimasu}}

goal.t: だんだん寒くなりましたね。
goal.r: Dandan samuku narimashita ne.
goal.tr: It's getting colder and colder, isn't it?

dialog.t: 最近、日本語が上手になりましたね。
dialog.r: Saikin, Nihongo ga jōzu ni narimashita ne.
dialog.tr: Your Japanese has really improved lately.

dialog.t: ありがとうございます。毎日勉強していますから。
dialog.r: Arigatō gozaimasu. Mainichi benkyō shite imasu kara.
dialog.tr: Thank you. I study every day.

dialog.t: ご注文は？
dialog.r: Go-chūmon wa?
dialog.tr: What would you like?

dialog.t: 私はコーヒーにします。
dialog.r: Watashi wa kōhī ni shimasu.
dialog.tr: I'll have coffee.

dialog.t: 暑くなりましたから、私はアイスティーにします。
dialog.r: Atsuku narimashita kara, watashi wa aisu tī ni shimasu.
dialog.tr: It's got hot, so I'll have an iced tea.

blocks.p: **Becoming: {{なります|narimasu}}.** An い-adjective changes {{い|i}} to {{く|ku}}: {{寒い|samui}} → {{寒くなります|samuku narimasu}} “it gets cold”. A な-adjective or a noun takes {{に|ni}}: {{上手になります|jōzu ni narimasu}} “get good at”, {{医者になります|isha ni narimasu}} “become a doctor”. In the past, {{なりました|narimashita}} often means “has become”: {{寒くなりました|samuku narimashita}} “It's got cold”.

**Making: {{します|shimasu}}.** The same shapes with {{します|shimasu}} mean “make something…”: {{部屋をきれいにします|heya o kirei ni shimasu}} “I'll tidy the room” (make it clean), {{音を小さくしてください|oto o chiisaku shite kudasai}} “Please turn the sound down” (make it small).

**Choosing: noun + {{にします|ni shimasu}}.** In shops and restaurants: {{コーヒーにします|kōhī ni shimasu}} “I'll have coffee”, {{これにします|kore ni shimasu}} “I'll take this one”. Word for word “I make it coffee”: the most natural way to say what you've decided on.

ex.t: 将来、医者になりたいです。
ex.r: Shōrai, isha ni naritai desu.
ex.tr: I want to become a doctor in the future.

ex.t: 薬を飲んで、元気になりました。
ex.r: Kusuri o nonde, genki ni narimashita.
ex.tr: I took some medicine and got better.

ex.t: 日本語が上手になりたいです。
ex.r: Nihongo ga jōzu ni naritai desu.
ex.tr: I want to get good at Japanese.

ex.t: 部屋をきれいにしてください。
ex.r: Heya o kirei ni shite kudasai.
ex.tr: Please tidy your room.

ex.t: 私はこのケーキにします。
ex.r: Watashi wa kono kēki ni shimasu.
ex.tr: I'll have this cake.

ex.t: 来月から、バスの料金が高くなります。
ex.r: Raigetsu kara, basu no ryōkin ga takaku narimasu.
ex.tr: Bus fares are going up from next month.

blocks.tip: {{～になりました|… ni narimashita}} is also how polite Japanese announces news: {{会議は三時からになりました|kaigi wa san-ji kara ni narimashita}} “The meeting will now start at three”.

mistakes.why: An い-adjective changes {{い|i}} to {{く|ku}} before {{なります|narimasu}}.
A な-adjective takes {{に|ni}}: {{元気になりました|genki ni narimashita}}.
Choosing is {{にします|ni shimasu}}; {{をします|o shimasu}} would mean “do coffee”.

practice.why: An い-adjective: {{暑く|atsuku}} + {{なりました|narimashita}}.

{{チーズケーキになります。|Chīzukēki ni narimasu.}}

practice.r: Nihongo ga jōzu ni naritai desu.

practice.q: Your turn: how have you, your town or your life changed recently? Use {{なりました|narimashita}}.

answers.t: 最近、仕事が忙しくなりました。でも、料理が上手になりました。
answers.r: Saikin, shigoto ga isogashiku narimashita. Demo, ryōri ga jōzu ni narimashita.
answers.tr: Work has got busy lately. But I've got good at cooking.

answers.t: 私の町は新しい駅ができて、便利になりました。
answers.r: Watashi no machi wa atarashii eki ga dekite, benri ni narimashita.
answers.tr: A new station opened in my town, and it's become convenient.

lessons.title: Say what you must and needn't do
lessons.summary: Talk about what you have to do and what's optional: “I have to get up early tomorrow.” “You don't need to bring anything.”
lessons.topic: {{～なければなりません|… nakereba narimasen}} and casual {{～なきゃ|… nakya}}; {{～なくてもいいです|… nakute mo ii desu}}

goal.t: 明日は早く起きなければなりません。
goal.r: Ashita wa hayaku okinakereba narimasen.
goal.tr: I have to get up early tomorrow.

dialog.t: 土曜日のパーティーに、何か持っていかなければなりませんか。
dialog.r: Doyōbi no pātī ni, nanika motte ikanakereba narimasen ka.
dialog.tr: Do I need to bring anything to the party on Saturday?

dialog.t: いいえ、何も持ってこなくてもいいですよ。
dialog.r: Iie, nani mo motte konakute mo ii desu yo.
dialog.tr: No, you don't need to bring anything.

dialog.t: 何時に行かなければなりませんか。
dialog.r: Nan-ji ni ikanakereba narimasen ka.
dialog.tr: What time do I need to be there?

dialog.t: 七時ごろ来てください。あ、靴を脱がなければなりませんから、きれいな靴下で来てくださいね！
dialog.r: Shichi-ji goro kite kudasai. A, kutsu o nuganakereba narimasen kara, kirei na kutsushita de kite kudasai ne!
dialog.tr: Please come around seven. Oh, and you'll have to take your shoes off, so wear clean socks!

blocks.p: **Must: the ない form + {{なければなりません|nakereba narimasen}}.** Change the final {{ない|nai}} to {{なければなりません|nakereba narimasen}}: {{行かない|ikanai}} → {{行かなければなりません|ikanakereba narimasen}} “I have to go”. Word for word “if I don't go, it won't do”: a double negative that means “must”. It's long, but completely regular.

**In everyday speech** it gets shorter: {{行かなきゃ|ikanakya}} with friends (“gotta go”), or {{行かなければいけません|ikanakereba ikemasen}}, which means the same as {{なりません|narimasen}}. You'll hear {{なきゃ|nakya}} all the time.

**Don't have to: the ない form + {{くてもいいです|kute mo ii desu}}.** {{ない|nai}} → {{なくてもいいです|nakute mo ii desu}}: {{行かなくてもいいです|ikanakute mo ii desu}} “You don't have to go”. It's the permission pattern you know ({{てもいい|te mo ii}}) on a negative: “it's fine even if you don't go”.

table: {{書かなければなりません|kakanakereba narimasen}}
{{書かなくてもいいです|kakanakute mo ii desu}}
You don't have to write it.
{{書かなければなりませんか|kakanakereba narimasen ka}}
Do I have to write it?

blocks.p: Careful: “mustn't” is a different pattern, the rule from the permission lesson: {{書いてはいけません|kaite wa ikemasen}} “You mustn't write it”.

ex.t: 薬を飲まなければなりません。
ex.r: Kusuri o nomanakereba narimasen.
ex.tr: I have to take medicine.

ex.t: もう帰らなきゃ。
ex.r: Mō kaeranakya.
ex.tr: I've got to go home now.

ex.t: 日曜日は会社へ行かなくてもいいです。
ex.r: Nichiyōbi wa kaisha e ikanakute mo ii desu.
ex.tr: I don't have to go to the office on Sundays.

ex.t: 名前を書かなければなりませんか。
ex.r: Namae o kakanakereba narimasen ka.
ex.tr: Do I have to write my name?

ex.t: いいえ、書かなくてもいいですよ。
ex.r: Iie, kakanakute mo ii desu yo.
ex.tr: No, you don't need to.

ex.t: 日本では、家に入る前に靴を脱がなければなりません。
ex.r: Nihon de wa, ie ni hairu mae ni kutsu o nuganakereba narimasen.
ex.tr: In Japan, you have to take your shoes off before going into a house.

blocks.tip: The shortest everyday form is {{～ないと|… nai to}}: {{もう行かないと|mō ikanai to}} “I have to get going”.

mistakes.wrong: 行くなければなりません。
mistakes.right: 行かなければなりません。
mistakes.why: Start from the ない form: {{行かない|ikanai}} → {{行かなければ|ikanakereba}}.

mistakes.wrong: 書かないてもいいです。
mistakes.right: 書かなくてもいいです。
mistakes.tr: You don't have to write it.
mistakes.why: {{ない|nai}} changes like an い-adjective: {{なくて|nakute}}, then {{もいいです|mo ii desu}}.

practice.q: Choose the missing ending.
practice.t: 明日は六時に起き___なりません。
practice.r: Ashita wa roku-ji ni oki___ narimasen.
practice.tr: I have to get up at six tomorrow.

practice.why: {{なくてもいい|nakute mo ii}}: it's fine not to.

lines.r: Konban, eiga o mi ni ikanai?

practice.q: Your turn: say two things you have to do this week, and one thing you don't have to do.

answers.t: 今週は宿題を出さなければなりません。歯医者にも行かなければなりません。でも、土曜日は働かなくてもいいです。
answers.r: Konshū wa shukudai o dasanakereba narimasen. Haisha ni mo ikanakereba narimasen. Demo, doyōbi wa hatarakanakute mo ii desu.
answers.tr: This week I have to hand in my homework. I also have to go to the dentist. But I don't have to work on Saturday.

answers.r: Maiasa, inu no sanpo o shinakereba narimasen. Ryōri wa shinakute mo ii desu.
answers.tr: Every morning I have to walk the dog. I don't have to cook.

lessons.title: Give advice
lessons.summary: Tell someone what they'd better do or not do, and ask people not to do things: “You'd better go home and rest.” “Please don't worry.”
lessons.topic: {{～たほうがいいです|… ta hō ga ii desu}}; {{～ないほうがいいです|… nai hō ga ii desu}}; {{～ないでください|… naide kudasai}}

goal.t: 今日は早く帰って、休んだほうがいいですよ。
goal.r: Kyō wa hayaku kaette, yasunda hō ga ii desu yo.
goal.tr: You'd better go home early today and rest.

dialog.t: 大丈夫ですか。顔色が悪いですよ。
dialog.r: Daijōbu desu ka. Kaoiro ga warui desu yo.
dialog.tr: Are you OK? You look pale.

dialog.t: 昨日から熱があるんです。
dialog.r: Kinō kara netsu ga aru n desu.
dialog.tr: I've had a fever since yesterday.

dialog.t: それは大変ですね。今日は早く帰って、休んだほうがいいですよ。
dialog.r: Sore wa taihen desu ne. Kyō wa hayaku kaette, yasunda hō ga ii desu yo.
dialog.tr: Oh no. You'd better go home early today and rest.

dialog.t: でも、仕事が…。
dialog.r: Demo, shigoto ga…
dialog.tr: But my work…

dialog.t: 仕事は心配しないでください。私がやりますから。
dialog.r: Shigoto wa shinpai shinaide kudasai. Watashi ga yarimasu kara.
dialog.tr: Don't worry about the work. I'll do it.

blocks.p: **You'd better: plain past + {{ほうがいいです|hō ga ii desu}}.** {{休んだほうがいいです|yasunda hō ga ii desu}} “You'd better rest”, word for word “the side of having rested is good”. The verb is in the plain past, even though the advice is about now or later. It's strong, friendly advice; {{よ|yo}} at the end makes it warmer.
**You'd better not: the ない form + {{ほうがいいです|hō ga ii desu}}.** Here the verb is in the ない form, not the past: {{あまり飲まないほうがいいです|amari nomanai hō ga ii desu}} “You'd better not drink too much”.

**Please don't: the ない form + {{でください|de kudasai}}.** {{心配しないでください|shinpai shinaide kudasai}} “Please don't worry”, {{ここに車を止めないでください|koko ni kuruma o tomenaide kudasai}} “Please don't park here”. It's the negative partner of {{てください|te kudasai}}.

table: {{寝たほうがいいです|neta hō ga ii desu}}
{{食べないほうがいいです|tabenai hō ga ii desu}}

blocks.p: Advising your boss or your teacher is delicate. Instead of telling them, ask: {{少し休みませんか|sukoshi yasumimasen ka}} “Shall we take a short break?”

ex.t: 傘を持っていったほうがいいですよ。
ex.r: Kasa o motte itta hō ga ii desu yo.
ex.tr: You'd better take an umbrella.

ex.t: 夜遅くコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。
ex.r: Yoru osoku kōhī o nomanai hō ga ii desu.
ex.tr: You'd better not drink coffee late at night.

ex.t: 心配しないでください。
ex.r: Shinpai shinaide kudasai.
ex.tr: Please don't worry.

ex.t: ここで写真を撮らないでください。
ex.r: Koko de shashin o toranaide kudasai.
ex.tr: Please don't take photos here.

ex.t: 毎日少し勉強したほうがいいと思います。
ex.r: Mainichi sukoshi benkyō shita hō ga ii to omoimasu.
ex.tr: I think it's better to study a little every day.

ex.t: 病院へ行ったほうがいいですよ。
ex.r: Byōin e itta hō ga ii desu yo.
ex.tr: You should see a doctor.

blocks.tip: {{ほうがいい|hō ga ii}} is real advice, with a reason behind it. A gentler suggestion, {{～たらどうですか|… tara dō desu ka}}, comes in a later lesson.

mistakes.wrong: 飲まなかったほうがいいです。
mistakes.right: 飲まないほうがいいです。
mistakes.why: For “better not”, use the ない form, not the past.

mistakes.wrong: 心配しなくてください。
mistakes.right: 心配しないでください。
mistakes.why: “Please don't” is {{ないでください|naide kudasai}}; {{なくて|nakute}} belongs to {{なくてもいい|nakute mo ii}} “needn't”.

practice.q: Choose the missing ending.
practice.t: 早く寝___ほうがいいですよ。
practice.r: Hayaku ne___ hō ga ii desu yo.
practice.tr: You'd better go to bed early.
practice.why: Advice: plain past + {{ほうがいい|hō ga ii}}: {{寝たほうがいい|neta hō ga ii}}.

practice.q: Choose the missing ending.

practice.r: Koko ni kuruma o tome___ kudasai.
practice.tr: Please don't park here.
practice.why: “Please don't”: {{止めないでください|tomenaide kudasai}}.

options: {{今日は行かないほうがいいですよ。|Kyō wa ikanai hō ga ii desu yo.}}
{{今日は行かなかったほうがいいですよ。|Kyō wa ikanakatta hō ga ii desu yo.}}
{{今日は行ったほうがいいですよ。|Kyō wa itta hō ga ii desu yo.}}
practice.why: “Better not”: the ない form + {{ほうがいい|hō ga ii}}.

practice.q: A friend can't sleep well. Choose your advice.

lines.t: 最近、よく眠れないんです。
lines.r: Saikin, yoku nemurenai n desu.
lines.tr: I haven't been sleeping well lately.

options: 寝る前に、スマホを見ないほうがいいですよ。
寝る前に、スマホを見なかったほうがいいですよ。
rs: Neru mae ni, sumaho o minai hō ga ii desu yo.
Neru mae ni, sumaho o minakatta hō ga ii desu yo.
lines.why: “Better not”: {{見ないほうがいい|minai hō ga ii}}.

lines.t: そうですね。ほかには？
lines.r: Sō desu ne. Hoka ni wa?
lines.tr: Good point. Anything else?

options: 夜はコーヒーを飲まないでください。
夜はコーヒーを飲まなくてください。
rs: Yoru wa kōhī o nomanaide kudasai.
Yoru wa kōhī o nomanakute kudasai.
lines.why: “Don't…, please”: {{ないでください|naide kudasai}}.

lessons.title: Say when things happen
lessons.summary: Say when something happens or happened: “When I was a child, I lived in Osaka.” “When it's cold, I drink hot tea.”
lessons.topic: plain form + {{とき|toki}}; {{子供のとき|kodomo no toki}}; {{行くとき|iku toki}} and {{行ったとき|itta toki}}

goal.t: 子供のとき、大阪に住んでいました。
goal.r: Kodomo no toki, Ōsaka ni sunde imashita.
goal.tr: When I was a child, I lived in Osaka.

dialog.t: トムさんはいつ日本語の勉強を始めましたか。
dialog.r: Tomu-san wa itsu Nihongo no benkyō o hajimemashita ka.
dialog.tr: When did you start learning Japanese, Tom?

dialog.t: 高校生のとき、始めました。
dialog.r: Kōkōsei no toki, hajimemashita.
dialog.tr: When I was in high school.

dialog.t: どうして日本語を？
dialog.r: Dōshite Nihongo o?
dialog.tr: Why Japanese?

dialog.t: 十五歳のとき、家族と日本へ来たんです。その時、日本が大好きになりました。
dialog.r: Jūgo-sai no toki, kazoku to Nihon e kita n desu. Sono toki, Nihon ga daisuki ni narimashita.
dialog.tr: When I was fifteen, I came to Japan with my family. That's when I fell in love with Japan.

blocks.p: **When: … {{とき|toki}}.** {{とき|toki}} is a noun meaning “time”, so whatever describes it comes before it, just as a description comes before any noun: a noun + {{の|no}} ({{子供のとき|kodomo no toki}} “when I was a child”), an い-adjective ({{寒いとき|samui toki}} “when it's cold”), a な-adjective + {{な|na}} ({{ひまなとき|hima na toki}} “when I'm free”), a plain verb ({{寝るとき|neru toki}} “when I go to bed”).

**The order of events decides the verb before {{とき|toki}}.** The tense of the whole sentence is at the end. The verb before {{とき|toki}} is in the dictionary form if that action hasn't happened yet at that moment, and in the past if it already has:

table: {{日本へ行くとき、カメラを買いました。|Nihon e iku toki, kamera o kaimashita.}}
I bought a camera before going to Japan (on my way).
{{日本へ行ったとき、カメラを買いました。|Nihon e itta toki, kamera o kaimashita.}}
I bought a camera when I went to Japan (once I was there).

blocks.p: **A subject inside the とき part takes {{が|ga}}**, not {{は|wa}}: {{母が来たとき|haha ga kita toki}} “when my mother came”. {{は|wa}} stays for the topic of the whole sentence.

ex.t: ひまなとき、何をしますか。
ex.r: Hima na toki, nani o shimasu ka.
ex.tr: What do you do when you're free?

ex.t: 寒いとき、温かいお茶を飲みます。
ex.r: Samui toki, atatakai ocha o nomimasu.
ex.tr: When it's cold, I drink hot tea.

ex.t: 日本へ行くとき、ガイドブックを買いました。
ex.r: Nihon e iku toki, gaidobukku o kaimashita.
ex.tr: I bought a guidebook before going to Japan.

ex.t: 家に帰ったとき、だれもいませんでした。
ex.r: Ie ni kaetta toki, dare mo imasen deshita.
ex.tr: When I got home, nobody was there.

ex.t: 母が来たとき、一緒に京都へ行きました。
ex.r: Haha ga kita toki, issho ni Kyōto e ikimashita.
ex.tr: When my mother came, we went to Kyoto together.

ex.t: 寝るとき、「おやすみなさい」と言います。
ex.r: Neru toki, 'oyasuminasai' to iimasu.
ex.tr: When you go to bed, you say “oyasuminasai” (good night).

blocks.tip: {{寝る前に|neru mae ni}} “before going to bed” and {{寝るとき|neru toki}} “at bedtime” are close: {{とき|toki}} is about the moment, {{前に|mae ni}} about the order.

mistakes.wrong: 子供とき、大阪に住んでいました。
mistakes.right: 子供のとき、大阪に住んでいました。
mistakes.rw: Kodomo toki, Ōsaka ni sunde imashita.
mistakes.rr: Kodomo no toki, Ōsaka ni sunde imashita.
mistakes.tr: When I was a child, I lived in Osaka.
mistakes.why: A noun needs {{の|no}} before {{とき|toki}}.

mistakes.wrong: ひまとき、本を読みます。
mistakes.right: ひまなとき、本を読みます。
mistakes.rr: Hima na toki, hon o yomimasu.
mistakes.why: A な-adjective takes {{な|na}} before {{とき|toki}}.

mistakes.wrong: 日本へ行ったとき、パスポートを取りました。
mistakes.right: 日本へ行くとき、パスポートを取りました。
mistakes.rw: Nihon e itta toki, pasupōto o torimashita.
mistakes.rr: Nihon e iku toki, pasupōto o torimashita.
mistakes.tr: I got a passport before going to Japan.
mistakes.why: The passport came before the trip, so the trip hadn't happened yet: {{行くとき|iku toki}}.

lessons.title: Give and follow directions
lessons.summary: Tell someone the way, and understand directions: “Go straight on, and the station is on your right.”
lessons.topic: dictionary form + {{と|to}} “whenever, and then”; {{を|o}} for the route; {{に曲がる|ni magaru}}

goal.t: まっすぐ行くと、右に駅があります。
goal.r: Massugu iku to, migi ni eki ga arimasu.
goal.tr: Go straight on, and the station is on your right.

dialog.t: すみません、市役所へ行きたいんですが…。
dialog.r: Sumimasen, shiyakusho e ikitai n desu ga…
dialog.tr: Excuse me, I'd like to get to the city hall…

dialog.t: 市役所ですか。この道をまっすぐ行ってください。二つ目の信号を左に曲がると、銀行があります。
dialog.r: Shiyakusho desu ka. Kono michi o massugu itte kudasai. Futatsume no shingō o hidari ni magaru to, ginkō ga arimasu.
dialog.tr: City hall? Go straight along this road. Turn left at the second traffic lights, and there's a bank.

dialog.t: 二つ目の信号を左ですね。
dialog.r: Futatsume no shingō o hidari desu ne.
dialog.tr: Left at the second lights, right?

dialog.t: はい。市役所は銀行の隣ですよ。
dialog.r: Hai. Shiyakusho wa ginkō no tonari desu yo.
dialog.tr: Yes. The city hall is next to the bank.

dialog.t: ありがとうございました。
dialog.r: Arigatō gozaimashita.
dialog.tr: Thank you very much.

blocks.p: **Whenever, and then: dictionary form + {{と|to}}.** After a dictionary form, {{と|to}} means: when this happens, that always follows. It's perfect for directions: {{まっすぐ行くと、右に駅があります|massugu iku to, migi ni eki ga arimasu}} “Go straight on, and there's the station on your right”. It also works for machines and nature: {{このボタンを押すと、お湯が出ます|kono botan o osu to, oyu ga demasu}} “When you press this button, hot water comes out”. What follows {{と|to}} is a result, never a request or a wish.

**The route takes {{を|o}}.** With verbs of moving, {{を|o}} marks the space you go along or through: {{この道をまっすぐ行きます|kono michi o massugu ikimasu}} “go straight along this road”, {{橋を渡ります|hashi o watarimasu}} “cross the bridge”, {{角を曲がります|kado o magarimasu}} “turn at the corner”. The direction takes {{に|ni}}: {{右に曲がります|migi ni magarimasu}} “turn right”.

table: {{この道を行きます|kono michi o ikimasu}}
{{信号を右に曲がります|shingō o migi ni magarimasu}}
{{～と、左にあります|… to, hidari ni arimasu}}

blocks.p: Counting in order: {{一つ目|hitotsume}} “the first”, {{二つ目|futatsume}} “the second”: {{二つ目の角|futatsume no kado}} “the second corner”.

ex.t: この道をまっすぐ行ってください。
ex.r: Kono michi o massugu itte kudasai.
ex.tr: Go straight along this road.

ex.t: 二つ目の角を右に曲がってください。
ex.r: Futatsume no kado o migi ni magatte kudasai.
ex.tr: Turn right at the second corner.

ex.t: 橋を渡ると、左に郵便局があります。
ex.r: Hashi o wataru to, hidari ni yūbinkyoku ga arimasu.
ex.tr: Cross the bridge, and there's the post office on your left.

ex.t: このボタンを押すと、切符が出ます。
ex.r: Kono botan o osu to, kippu ga demasu.
ex.tr: When you press this button, the ticket comes out.

ex.t: 春になると、桜が咲きます。
ex.r: Haru ni naru to, sakura ga sakimasu.
ex.tr: When spring comes, the cherry trees blossom.

ex.t: 駅から歩いて五分ぐらいです。
ex.r: Eki kara aruite go-fun gurai desu.
ex.tr: It's about five minutes' walk from the station.

blocks.tip: To check directions, repeat the key part with {{ね|ne}}: {{二つ目の信号を左ですね|futatsume no shingō o hidari desu ne}} “Left at the second lights, right?”.

mistakes.wrong: まっすぐ行くと、右に曲がってください。
mistakes.right: まっすぐ行って、右に曲がってください。
mistakes.rw: Massugu iku to, migi ni magatte kudasai.
mistakes.rr: Massugu itte, migi ni magatte kudasai.
mistakes.tr: Go straight on, then turn right.
mistakes.why: After {{と|to}} comes a result, never a request. For a string of instructions, use the て-form.
The space you cross or go along takes {{を|o}}.

lessons.title: Talk about giving and getting presents
lessons.summary: Say who gave what to whom: “I gave my mother flowers.” “A friend gave me a book.” “I got a watch from my father.”
lessons.topic: {{あげます|agemasu}}, {{くれます|kuremasu}}, {{もらいます|moraimasu}}

goal.t: 誕生日に友達が本をくれました。
goal.r: Tanjōbi ni tomodachi ga hon o kuremashita.
goal.tr: A friend gave me a book for my birthday.

dialog.t: すてきな時計ですね。
dialog.r: Suteki na tokei desu ne.
dialog.tr: What a lovely watch.

dialog.t: ありがとう。誕生日に父にもらったんです。
dialog.r: Arigatō. Tanjōbi ni chichi ni moratta n desu.
dialog.tr: Thanks. I got it from my father for my birthday.

dialog.t: いいですね。お父さんに何かあげましたか。
dialog.r: Ii desu ne. Otōsan ni nanika agemashita ka.
dialog.tr: Nice. Did you give your father anything?

dialog.t: 父の日にネクタイをあげました。ゆいさんは、誕生日に何をもらいましたか。
dialog.r: Chichi no hi ni nekutai o agemashita. Yui-san wa, tanjōbi ni nani o moraimashita ka.
dialog.tr: I gave him a tie on Father's Day. What did you get for your birthday, Yui?

dialog.t: 姉がかわいいかばんをくれました。
dialog.r: Ane ga kawaii kaban o kuremashita.
dialog.tr: My sister gave me a cute bag.

blocks.p: **Three verbs, chosen by direction.** English has “give” and “get”; Japanese chooses the verb by who gives to whom, seen from where you stand:

table: I (or anyone) give to someone else: away from me
{{私は母に花をあげました。|Watashi wa haha ni hana o agemashita.}} I gave my mother flowers.
someone gives to me or my family: towards me
{{友達が本をくれました。|Tomodachi ga hon o kuremashita.}} A friend gave me a book.
{{父に時計をもらいました。|Chichi ni tokei o moraimashita.}} I got a watch from my father.

blocks.p: The receiver takes {{に|ni}} with {{あげます|agemasu}} and {{くれます|kuremasu}}. With {{もらいます|moraimasu}}, the giver takes {{に|ni}}, or {{から|kara}} “from”. After {{くれます|kuremasu}}, “to me” is usually left out: {{くれます|kuremasu}} already says it.

**The key rule:** when something is given **to you**, never use {{あげます|agemasu}}: {{友達が私に本をあげました|tomodachi ga watashi ni hon o agemashita}} is wrong. Use {{くれます|kuremasu}}, or turn the sentence round with {{もらいます|moraimasu}}: {{友達に本をもらいました|tomodachi ni hon o moraimashita}}.

**Family words.** Talking to others about your own family, Japanese uses plain words: {{父|chichi}} my father, {{母|haha}} my mother, {{姉|ane}} my older sister. For someone else's family, or talking to your own parents, the polite words: {{お父さん|otōsan}}, {{お母さん|okāsan}}, {{お姉さん|onēsan}}.

ex.t: 私は母に花をあげました。
ex.r: Watashi wa haha ni hana o agemashita.
ex.tr: I gave my mother flowers.

ex.t: 父に時計をもらいました。
ex.r: Chichi ni tokei o moraimashita.
ex.tr: I got a watch from my father.

ex.t: 田中さんは佐藤さんにチョコレートをあげました。
ex.r: Tanaka-san wa Satō-san ni chokorēto o agemashita.
ex.tr: Mr Tanaka gave Ms Sato some chocolates.

ex.t: このペン、だれがくれたんですか。
ex.r: Kono pen, dare ga kureta n desu ka.
ex.tr: Who gave you this pen?

ex.t: 先生から手紙をもらいました。
ex.r: Sensei kara tegami o moraimashita.
ex.tr: I got a letter from my teacher.

ex.t: これ、どうぞ。京都のお土産です。
ex.r: Kore, dōzo. Kyōto no omiyage desu.
ex.tr: This is for you. A souvenir from Kyoto.

blocks.tip: In Japan, people often bring {{お土産|omiyage}}, small gifts from a trip, for colleagues and friends. Hand one over with {{これ、どうぞ|kore, dōzo}} “This is for you”.

mistakes.why: Someone giving to you: {{くれます|kuremasu}}, never {{あげます|agemasu}}.

mistakes.tr: I got a watch from my father.

lessons.title: Ask for and talk about favours
lessons.summary: Ask someone to do something for you, softly, and talk about kindness: “Could you check this for me?” “Ken helped me move.”
lessons.topic: {{～てあげます|… te agemasu}}, {{～てくれます|… te kuremasu}}, {{～てもらいます|… te moraimasu}}; {{～てもらえませんか|… te moraemasen ka}}

goal.t: すみません、写真を撮ってもらえませんか。
goal.r: Sumimasen, shashin o totte moraemasen ka.
goal.tr: Excuse me, could you take a photo for us?

dialog.t: 田中さん、ちょっといいですか。この書類をチェックしてもらえませんか。
dialog.r: Tanaka-san, chotto ii desu ka. Kono shorui o chekku shite moraemasen ka.
dialog.tr: Mr Tanaka, have you got a moment? Could you check this document for me?

dialog.t: いいですよ。…はい、大丈夫です。
dialog.r: Ii desu yo. … Hai, daijōbu desu.
dialog.tr: Sure. …Yes, it's fine.

dialog.t: ありがとうございます。助かりました。
dialog.r: Arigatō gozaimasu. Tasukarimashita.
dialog.tr: Thank you. That's a great help.

dialog.t: いいえ。昨日はコピーを手伝ってくれて、ありがとう。
dialog.r: Iie. Kinō wa kopī o tetsudatte kurete, arigatō.
dialog.tr: Not at all. And thanks for helping me with the copying yesterday.

blocks.p: **Doing things for people.** The three giving verbs from the last lesson go after a て-form to show that an action is a favour, with the same directions:

table: {{弟に宿題を教えてあげました。|Otōto ni shukudai o oshiete agemashita.}} I helped my little brother with his homework.
{{ケンが引っ越しを手伝ってくれました。|Ken ga hikkoshi o tetsudatte kuremashita.}} Ken helped me move.
I get someone to do something
{{友達に写真を撮ってもらいました。|Tomodachi ni shashin o totte moraimashita.}} I had a friend take my photo.

blocks.p: {{てくれます|te kuremasu}} is how Japanese shows gratitude. {{手伝いました|tetsudaimashita}} just reports that he helped; {{手伝ってくれました|tetsudatte kuremashita}} says he helped **me**, and I'm grateful. Leaving it out can sound cold. {{てあげます|te agemasu}}, on the other hand, can sound like showing off: don't say {{手伝ってあげます|tetsudatte agemasu}} to someone's face. Offer with {{手伝いましょうか|tetsudaimashō ka}} instead.

**Asking for a favour.** Softer than {{てください|te kudasai}}: {{～てくれませんか|… te kuremasen ka}} “Would you… for me?”, and softest of all, {{～てもらえませんか|… te moraemasen ka}} “Could I ask you to…?”. Start with {{すみません|sumimasen}} for strangers, or {{ちょっといいですか|chotto ii desu ka}} “Have you got a moment?” for colleagues.
**Saying thank you for a favour:** the て-form of {{くれる|kureru}} + {{ありがとう|arigatō}}: {{手伝ってくれて、ありがとう|tetsudatte kurete, arigatō}} “Thanks for helping me”.

ex.t: 母が駅まで車で送ってくれました。
ex.r: Haha ga eki made kuruma de okutte kuremashita.
ex.tr: My mother drove me to the station.

ex.t: 友達に日本語を教えてもらっています。
ex.r: Tomodachi ni Nihongo o oshiete moratte imasu.
ex.tr: A friend is teaching me Japanese.

ex.t: 妹にケーキを作ってあげました。
ex.r: Imōto ni kēki o tsukutte agemashita.
ex.tr: I made a cake for my little sister.

ex.t: ちょっと窓を開けてくれませんか。
ex.r: Chotto mado o akete kuremasen ka.
ex.tr: Would you open the window a little?

ex.t: すみません、道を教えてもらえませんか。
ex.r: Sumimasen, michi o oshiete moraemasen ka.
ex.tr: Excuse me, could you tell me the way?

ex.t: 来てくれて、ありがとう。
ex.r: Kite kurete, arigatō.
ex.tr: Thanks for coming.

blocks.tip: {{助かりました|tasukarimashita}} “That was a great help”, word for word “I was saved”, is the warmest thank-you for a favour.

mistakes.wrong: ケンが私を手伝ってあげました。
mistakes.right: ケンが手伝ってくれました。
mistakes.rw: Ken ga watashi o tetsudatte agemashita.
mistakes.why: Someone doing something for you: {{てくれます|te kuremasu}}. {{てあげます|te agemasu}} is for favours going away from you.

lessons.title: Describe people and things in detail
lessons.summary: Describe with whole sentences: “the movie I saw yesterday”, “the person wearing glasses”, “the cake my mother made”.
lessons.topic: clauses before the noun: {{昨日見た映画|kinō mita eiga}}; {{が|ga}} inside them

goal.t: 昨日見た映画はとてもおもしろかったです。
goal.r: Kinō mita eiga wa totemo omoshirokatta desu.
goal.tr: The movie I saw yesterday was really good.

dialog.t: あの眼鏡をかけている人はだれですか。
dialog.r: Ano megane o kakete iru hito wa dare desu ka.
dialog.tr: Who's that person wearing glasses?

dialog.t: 私が先週話した友達です。
dialog.r: Watashi ga senshū hanashita tomodachi desu.
dialog.tr: That's the friend I told you about last week.

dialog.t: ああ、大阪で働いている人ですか。
dialog.r: Ā, Ōsaka de hataraite iru hito desu ka.
dialog.tr: Oh, the one who works in Osaka?

dialog.t: そうです。このケーキも彼が作ったんですよ。
dialog.r: Sō desu. Kono kēki mo kare ga tsukutta n desu yo.
dialog.tr: That's right. He made this cake, too.

blocks.means: a small sentence inside a bigger one, with its own verb: [the movie] **I saw yesterday**.

blocks.p: **Describing with a sentence.** In English, a describing sentence comes after the noun: “the movie (that) I saw yesterday”. In Japanese it comes **before** the noun, like an adjective, with no word for “that” or “who”: {{昨日見た映画|kinō mita eiga}}, word for word “yesterday-saw movie”. The verb is in the plain form, right before the noun.

table: {{私は昨日映画を見ました。|Watashi wa kinō eiga o mimashita.}}
{{私が昨日見た映画|watashi ga kinō mita eiga}}
{{眼鏡をかけている人|megane o kakete iru hito}}
{{肉を食べない人|niku o tabenai hito}}

blocks.p: **Inside the clause, the subject takes {{が|ga}}**, never {{は|wa}}: {{母が作ったケーキ|haha ga tsukutta kēki}} “the cake my mother made” ({{の|no}} is also possible there: {{母の作ったケーキ|haha no tsukutta kēki}}). The whole thing then works as one big noun: {{母が作ったケーキはおいしいです|haha ga tsukutta kēki wa oishii desu}} “The cake my mother made is delicious”.

**Any plain form works**: present ({{よく行く店|yoku iku mise}} “the shop I often go to”), past ({{昨日買った本|kinō katta hon}} “the book I bought yesterday”), ている ({{あそこに立っている人|asoko ni tatte iru hito}} “the person standing over there”), negative ({{わからない言葉|wakaranai kotoba}} “words I don't understand”).

ex.t: 母が作ったケーキはおいしいです。
ex.r: Haha ga tsukutta kēki wa oishii desu.
ex.tr: The cake my mother made is delicious.

ex.t: あそこに立っている人は田中さんです。
ex.r: Asoko ni tatte iru hito wa Tanaka-san desu.
ex.tr: The person standing over there is Mr Tanaka.

ex.t: これは私がよく行く店です。
ex.r: Kore wa watashi ga yoku iku mise desu.
ex.tr: This is the shop I often go to.

ex.t: わからない言葉を辞書で調べました。
ex.r: Wakaranai kotoba o jisho de shirabemashita.
ex.tr: I looked up the words I didn't know in a dictionary.

ex.t: 日本で一番行きたい所はどこですか。
ex.r: Nihon de ichiban ikitai tokoro wa doko desu ka.
ex.tr: Where's the place you most want to go in Japan?

ex.t: 肉を食べない人もいます。
ex.r: Niku o tabenai hito mo imasu.
ex.tr: Some people don't eat meat.

blocks.tip: Long descriptions are normal in Japanese: {{去年京都で買った赤い着物|kyonen Kyōto de katta akai kimono}} “the red kimono I bought in Kyoto last year”. Find the noun at the end, then read the description backwards.

mistakes.wrong: 昨日見ました映画はおもしろかったです。

mistakes.rr: Kinō mita eiga wa omoshirokatta desu.
mistakes.tr: The movie I saw yesterday was good.
mistakes.why: The verb before a noun is in the plain form, never the ます form.

mistakes.rw: Haha wa tsukutta kēki wa oishii desu.
mistakes.rr: Haha ga tsukutta kēki wa oishii desu.
mistakes.tr: The cake my mother made is delicious.
mistakes.why: Inside a describing clause, the subject takes {{が|ga}} (or {{の|no}}), not {{は|wa}}.

lessons.title: Say what you can do, the short way
lessons.summary: Use the everyday “can” form: “I can speak a little Japanese.” “I still can't eat natto.” “Can you come tomorrow?”
lessons.topic: the potential form: {{話せる|hanaseru}}, {{食べられる|taberareru}}, {{来られる|korareru}}, {{できる|dekiru}}

goal.t: 日本語が少し話せます。
goal.r: Nihongo ga sukoshi hanasemasu.
goal.tr: I can speak a little Japanese.

dialog.t: 辛い物は食べられますか。
dialog.r: Karai mono wa taberaremasu ka.
dialog.tr: Can you eat spicy food?

dialog.t: はい、食べられます。でも、納豆はまだ食べられません。
dialog.r: Hai, taberaremasu. Demo, nattō wa mada taberaremasen.
dialog.tr: Yes, I can. But I still can't eat natto.

dialog.t: ははは。日本語が上手ですね。漢字も読めますか。
dialog.r: Hahaha. Nihongo ga jōzu desu ne. Kanji mo yomemasu ka.
dialog.tr: Ha ha. Your Japanese is very good. Can you read kanji too?

dialog.t: 少し読めます。でも、まだ書けません。
dialog.r: Sukoshi yomemasu. Demo, mada kakemasen.
dialog.tr: I can read a few. But I can't write them yet.

blocks.means: the form of a verb that means “can”: {{話せる|hanaseru}} “can speak”.

blocks.p: **One word for “can”.** Instead of {{ことができます|koto ga dekimasu}}, everyday Japanese changes the verb itself. **Group 1**: the u-sound at the end of the dictionary form becomes an e-sound + {{る|ru}}: {{話す|hanasu}} → {{話せる|hanaseru}} “can speak”, {{読む|yomu}} → {{読める|yomeru}}, {{行く|iku}} → {{行ける|ikeru}}. **Group 2**: {{る|ru}} → {{られる|rareru}}: {{食べる|taberu}} → {{食べられる|taberareru}}. **Group 3**: {{する|suru}} → {{できる|dekiru}}, {{来る|kuru}} → {{来られる|korareru}}.

The potential form is itself a group 2 verb: {{話せます|hanasemasu}}, {{話せない|hanasenai}} “can't speak”, {{話せなかった|hanasenakatta}} “couldn't speak”. **What you can do usually takes {{が|ga}}**, as with {{できます|dekimasu}}: {{日本語が話せます|Nihongo ga hanasemasu}}, {{漢字が読めます|kanji ga yomemasu}}.
In casual speech, group 2 verbs often drop the {{ら|ra}}: {{食べれる|tabereru}}, {{見れる|mireru}}. You'll hear it everywhere; in writing, use {{食べられる|taberareru}}.

ex.t: 辛い物は食べられません。
ex.r: Karai mono wa taberaremasen.
ex.tr: I can't eat spicy food.

ex.t: 明日のパーティーに来られますか。
ex.r: Ashita no pātī ni koraremasu ka.
ex.tr: Can you come to the party tomorrow?

ex.t: すみません、明日は行けません。
ex.r: Sumimasen, ashita wa ikemasen.
ex.tr: Sorry, I can't go tomorrow.

ex.t: この漢字が読めますか。
ex.r: Kono kanji ga yomemasu ka.
ex.tr: Can you read this kanji?

ex.t: 昨日はよく眠れませんでした。
ex.r: Kinō wa yoku nemuremasen deshita.
ex.tr: I couldn't sleep well last night.

ex.t: ここから富士山が見えます。
ex.r: Koko kara Fujisan ga miemasu.
ex.tr: You can see Mt Fuji from here.
ex.note: {{見えます|miemasu}}: “can be seen”, a special verb

blocks.tip: {{見える|mieru}} “can be seen” and {{聞こえる|kikoeru}} “can be heard” are special verbs for things that reach your eyes and ears by themselves. {{見られる|mirareru}} is “able to watch”: {{今晩、試合が見られます|konban, shiai ga miraremasu}} “I can watch the match tonight”.

mistakes.why: {{話す|hanasu}} is group 1: {{す|su}} → {{せる|seru}}. ({{話される|hanasareru}} is a different form, the passive.)
Group 1: {{行く|iku}} → {{行ける|ikeru}}. {{られる|rareru}} is only for group 2 verbs.

practice.why: Group 2: {{食べられる|taberareru}} → {{食べられません|taberaremasen}}.

practice.tr: Can you come to the party tomorrow?
practice.why: {{来る|kuru}} → {{来られる|korareru}}.

practice.q: Your manager asks about your Japanese. Choose your replies.

lines.r: Kanji ga yomemasu ka.

answers.r: Eigo to Furansugo ga hanasemasu. Ryōri mo dekimasu. Demo, nama no sakana wa taberaremasen.

lessons.title: Say what will happen if…
lessons.summary: Talk about conditions and what follows, and make gentle suggestions: “If it rains, I'll stay home.” “Why don't you ask the teacher?”
lessons.topic: {{～たら|… tara}} “if, when”; {{～たらどうですか|… tara dō desu ka}}

goal.t: 雨が降ったら、家で映画を見ます。
goal.r: Ame ga futtara, ie de eiga o mimasu.
goal.tr: If it rains, I'll watch a movie at home.

dialog.t: 明日、天気がよかったら、ピクニックに行きませんか。
dialog.r: Ashita, tenki ga yokattara, pikunikku ni ikimasen ka.
dialog.tr: If the weather's nice tomorrow, shall we go for a picnic?

dialog.t: いいですね。でも、雨が降ったら、どうしますか。
dialog.r: Ii desu ne. Demo, ame ga futtara, dō shimasu ka.
dialog.tr: Sounds good. But what shall we do if it rains?

dialog.t: 雨だったら、美術館に行きましょう。
dialog.r: Ame dattara, bijutsukan ni ikimashō.
dialog.tr: If it rains, let's go to a museum.

dialog.t: わかりました。駅に着いたら、電話しますね。
dialog.r: Wakarimashita. Eki ni tsuitara, denwa shimasu ne.
dialog.tr: OK. I'll call you when I get to the station.

blocks.p: **If…: the ta-form + {{ら|ra}}.** Take the plain past and add {{ら|ra}}: {{降った|futta}} → {{降ったら|futtara}} “if it rains”, {{よかった|yokatta}} → {{よかったら|yokattara}} “if it's good”, {{雨だった|ame datta}} → {{雨だったら|ame dattara}} “if it's rainy”, {{行かなかった|ikanakatta}} → {{行かなかったら|ikanakattara}} “if I don't go”. Despite the past form, it's usually about the future: the condition comes true first, then the rest follows.

**When, once…** If the first part is sure to happen, {{たら|tara}} means “when, once”: {{駅に着いたら、電話します|eki ni tsuitara, denwa shimasu}} “I'll call you when I get to the station”. Unlike {{と|to}}, anything can follow {{たら|tara}}: a plan, a request, an invitation.

**Suggesting: {{～たらどうですか|… tara dō desu ka}}** “How about…?”: {{先生に聞いたらどうですか|sensei ni kiitara dō desu ka}} “Why don't you ask the teacher?”. It's gentler than {{ほうがいい|hō ga ii}}; with friends, just {{聞いたら？|kiitara?}}.

ex.t: 安かったら、買います。
ex.r: Yasukattara, kaimasu.
ex.tr: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

ex.t: ひまだったら、手伝ってくれませんか。
ex.r: Hima dattara, tetsudatte kuremasen ka.
ex.tr: If you're free, could you help me?

ex.t: 日本に着いたら、メールしてください。
ex.r: Nihon ni tsuitara, mēru shite kudasai.
ex.tr: Please email me when you get to Japan.

ex.t: 宝くじが当たったら、何をしますか。
ex.r: Takarakuji ga atattara, nani o shimasu ka.

ex.note: {{よかったら|yokattara}} “if it's OK with you”: a very common soft opener

blocks.tip: {{たら|tara}} is the all-purpose “if, when” of everyday speech. When you're unsure which “if” to use, {{たら|tara}} is the safest choice.

mistakes.wrong: 雨が降るたら、行きません。

answers.t: 天気がよかったら、山に登ります。雨だったら、家で本を読みます。
answers.r: Tenki ga yokattara, yama ni noborimasu. Ame dattara, ie de hon o yomimasu.

lessons.title: Give conditions and recommendations
lessons.summary: Say what it takes for something to happen, and recommend things: “If you go by train, you'll get there in an hour.” “If it's Kyoto, go in autumn.”

goal.t: 京都なら、秋が一番きれいですよ。
goal.r: Kyōto nara, aki ga ichiban kirei desu yo.
goal.tr: If it's Kyoto you mean, autumn is the most beautiful time.

dialog.t: 来月、日本を旅行するんです。どこがいいですか。
dialog.r: Raigetsu, Nihon o ryokō suru n desu. Doko ga ii desu ka.
dialog.tr: I'm travelling around Japan next month. Where's good?

dialog.t: 温泉が好きなら、箱根がいいですよ。
dialog.r: Onsen ga suki nara, Hakone ga ii desu yo.
dialog.tr: If you like hot springs, Hakone is good.

dialog.t: 東京から遠いですか。
dialog.r: Tōkyō kara tōi desu ka.
dialog.tr: Is it far from Tokyo?

dialog.t: いいえ、電車で行けば、一時間半ぐらいで着きますよ。
dialog.r: Iie, densha de ikeba, ichi-jikan han gurai de tsukimasu yo.
dialog.tr: No, if you go by train, you'll get there in about an hour and a half.

dialog.t: どうすれば安く行けますか。
dialog.r: Dō sureba yasuku ikemasu ka.
dialog.tr: How can I get there cheaply?

dialog.t: フリーパスを買えば、安くなりますよ。
dialog.r: Furī pasu o kaeba, yasuku narimasu yo.
dialog.tr: If you buy a travel pass, it's cheaper.

blocks.p: **If (that's what it takes): the {{ば|ba}} form.** It puts the focus on the condition, what needs to happen for the result. Verbs: the final u-sound becomes an e-sound + {{ば|ba}}: {{行く|iku}} → {{行けば|ikeba}}, {{買う|kau}} → {{買えば|kaeba}}, {{食べる|taberu}} → {{食べれば|tabereba}}, {{する|suru}} → {{すれば|sureba}}, {{来る|kuru}} → {{来れば|kureba}}. い-adjectives: {{い|i}} → {{ければ|kereba}}: {{安ければ|yasukereba}}. Negatives: {{ない|nai}} → {{なければ|nakereba}}: the ending you met in {{なければなりません|nakereba narimasen}}.
{{どうすれば|dō sureba}} “what should I do to…?” is very useful: {{どうすればいいですか|dō sureba ii desu ka}} “What should I do?”

**If it's… (that you mean): {{なら|nara}}.** {{なら|nara}} picks up something the other person mentioned and adds advice or information about it: {{京都なら、秋がいいですよ|Kyōto nara, aki ga ii desu yo}} “If it's Kyoto, autumn's the time to go”. Nouns and な-adjectives go straight before it; verbs and い-adjectives in the plain form: {{温泉が好きなら|onsen ga suki nara}}, {{行くなら|iku nara}}, {{寒いなら|samui nara}}.

**Which one?** {{たら|tara}} is the everyday choice and works almost everywhere. {{ば|ba}} stresses the condition: “as long as…”, “all you need to do is…”. {{なら|nara}} responds to a topic someone has raised.

ex.t: 電車で行けば、一時間で着きます。
ex.r: Densha de ikeba, ichi-jikan de tsukimasu.
ex.tr: If you go by train, you'll get there in an hour.

ex.t: 安ければ、買いたいです。
ex.r: Yasukereba, kaitai desu.
ex.tr: If it's cheap, I'd like to buy it.

ex.t: どうすればいいですか。
ex.r: Dō sureba ii desu ka.
ex.tr: What should I do?

ex.t: 毎日練習すれば、上手になりますよ。
ex.r: Mainichi renshū sureba, jōzu ni narimasu yo.
ex.tr: If you practise every day, you'll get good.

ex.t: ラーメンなら、駅の前の店がおいしいですよ。
ex.r: Rāmen nara, eki no mae no mise ga oishii desu yo.
ex.tr: If it's ramen you want, the place in front of the station is good.

ex.t: 急がなければ、間に合いませんよ。
ex.r: Isoganakereba, maniaimasen yo.
ex.tr: If you don't hurry, you won't make it in time.

blocks.tip: A proverb: {{ちりも積もれば山となる|chiri mo tsumoreba yama to naru}} “Even dust, piled up, becomes a mountain”: a little study every day adds up!

mistakes.tr: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.
mistakes.why: An い-adjective: {{い|i}} → {{ければ|kereba}}.
Verbs: the last u-sound becomes an e-sound, then {{ば|ba}}: {{行く|iku}} → {{行けば|ikeba}}.

answers.t: おいしいピザなら、駅の近くの店が一番ですよ。早く行けば、待たなくてもいいです。
answers.r: Oishii piza nara, eki no chikaku no mise ga ichiban desu yo. Hayaku ikeba, matanakute mo ii desu.

lessons.title: Guess, and say how things look
lessons.summary: Say how things look, and make guesses: “That looks delicious!” “It'll probably rain tomorrow.” “He might be late.”
lessons.topic: {{～そうです|… sō desu}} “looks…”; {{～でしょう|… deshō}}; {{～かもしれません|… kamo shiremasen}}

goal.t: このケーキ、おいしそうですね！
goal.r: Kono kēki, oishisō desu ne!
goal.tr: This cake looks delicious!

dialog.t: このケーキ、おいしそうですね！
dialog.r: Kono kēki, oishisō desu ne!
dialog.tr: This cake looks delicious!

dialog.t: 一つどうぞ。あ、空が暗いですね。雨が降りそうです。
dialog.r: Hitotsu dōzo. A, sora ga kurai desu ne. Ame ga furisō desu.
dialog.tr: Have one. Oh, the sky's dark. It looks like it's going to rain.

dialog.t: ええ、夜は雨でしょう。
dialog.r: Ē, yoru wa ame deshō.
dialog.tr: Yes, it'll probably rain tonight.

dialog.t: 田中さん、遅いですね。
dialog.r: Tanaka-san, osoi desu ne.
dialog.tr: Mr Tanaka's late, isn't he?

dialog.t: 電車が遅れているかもしれませんね。
dialog.r: Densha ga okurete iru kamo shiremasen ne.
dialog.tr: Maybe his train's delayed.

blocks.p: **Looks…: {{そうです|sō desu}}.** For what you can see or sense right now. い-adjectives drop {{い|i}}: {{おいしい|oishii}} → {{おいしそうです|oishisō desu}} “it looks delicious”. な-adjectives just add it: {{元気そうです|genkisō desu}} “you look well”. Verbs use the stem: {{降ります|furimasu}} → {{雨が降りそうです|ame ga furisō desu}} “it looks like it's going to rain”. {{いい|ii}} becomes {{よさそう|yosasō}}. Before a noun: {{おいしそうなケーキ|oishisō na kēki}} “a delicious-looking cake”.

**Probably: plain form + {{でしょう|deshō}}.** A guess about something you can't see, fairly sure: {{明日は雨でしょう|ashita wa ame deshō}} “It'll probably rain tomorrow”, as weather forecasts say. Nouns and な-adjectives go straight before it, with no {{だ|da}}. With friends: {{だろう|darō}}.

**Maybe: plain form + {{かもしれません|kamo shiremasen}}.** Less sure: {{遅れるかもしれません|okureru kamo shiremasen}} “I might be late”. Again, nouns and な-adjectives go straight before it: {{雨かもしれません|ame kamo shiremasen}}. With friends: {{かも|kamo}}.

table: {{雨が降りそうです。|Ame ga furisō desu.}}
It looks like it's going to rain.
{{雨が降るでしょう。|Ame ga furu deshō.}}
{{雨が降るかもしれません。|Ame ga furu kamo shiremasen.}}

ex.t: 田中さんは元気そうでした。
ex.r: Tanaka-san wa genkisō deshita.
ex.tr: Mr Tanaka looked well.

ex.t: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
ex.r: Ashita wa hareru deshō.
ex.tr: It'll probably be sunny tomorrow.

ex.t: 会議に少し遅れるかもしれません。
ex.r: Kaigi ni sukoshi okureru kamo shiremasen.
ex.tr: I might be a little late for the meeting.

ex.t: あの人は先生かもしれません。
ex.r: Ano hito wa sensei kamo shiremasen.
ex.tr: That person might be a teacher.

ex.t: この本はおもしろそうです。
ex.r: Kono hon wa omoshirosō desu.
ex.tr: This book looks interesting.

ex.t: あのレストランはよさそうですね。
ex.r: Ano resutoran wa yosasō desu ne.
ex.tr: That restaurant looks good.

blocks.tip: {{そう|sō}} is for impressions, not for what's obvious. For a beautiful view right in front of you, just say {{きれいですね|kirei desu ne}}: {{きれいそう|kireisō}} isn't used for things you can plainly see.

mistakes.why: For “looks…”, drop the {{い|i}}: {{おいしそう|oishisō}}. ({{おいしいそうです|oishii sō desu}} means “I hear it's delicious”: the next lesson.)
Nouns go straight before {{かもしれません|kamo shiremasen}}: no {{だ|da}}.

practice.t: このラーメン、おいし___ですね。
practice.tr: This ramen looks delicious.

practice.r: Sora ga kurai desu ne. Ame ga furi___ desu.

practice.why: What you can see: stem + {{そうです|sō desu}}.

options: {{来るかもしれません。|Kuru kamo shiremasen.}}
practice.why: {{かもしれません|kamo shiremasen}}: “maybe”.

lines.tr: Yeah, I couldn't sleep much last night.

practice.q: Your turn: look out of the window. Say how things look, and guess what the weather will be like tomorrow.

answers.t: 空が暗くて、雨が降りそうです。明日も雨でしょう。
answers.r: Sora ga kurakute, ame ga furisō desu. Ashita mo ame deshō.
answers.tr: The sky is dark, and it looks like rain. It'll probably rain tomorrow too.

answers.r: Kyō wa totemo atatakasō desu. Ashita wa samuku naru kamo shiremasen.
answers.tr: It looks really warm today. It might get cold tomorrow.

lessons.title: Pass on what you've heard
lessons.summary: Report news and rumours: “I hear Mr Tanaka is getting married.” “Apparently the new café is good.”
lessons.topic: plain form + {{そうです|sō desu}} “I hear”; {{～って|… tte}}; {{～らしいです|… rashii desu}}

goal.t: 田中さんは来月結婚するそうです。
goal.r: Tanaka-san wa raigetsu kekkon suru sō desu.
goal.tr: I hear Mr Tanaka is getting married next month.

dialog.t: 聞きましたか。田中さん、来月結婚するそうですよ。
dialog.r: Kikimashita ka. Tanaka-san, raigetsu kekkon suru sō desu yo.
dialog.tr: Have you heard? Mr Tanaka is getting married next month.

dialog.t: え、本当ですか。相手はだれですか。
dialog.r: E, hontō desu ka. Aite wa dare desu ka.
dialog.tr: Really? Who to?

dialog.t: 大学の時の友達らしいです。
dialog.r: Daigaku no toki no tomodachi rashii desu.
dialog.tr: Apparently a friend from his university days.

dialog.t: そうですか。結婚式はどこでするんですか。
dialog.r: Sō desu ka. Kekkonshiki wa doko de suru n desu ka.
dialog.tr: I see. Where's the wedding?

dialog.t: 京都でするって。
dialog.r: Kyōto de suru tte.
dialog.tr: In Kyoto, he says.

blocks.p: **I hear…: plain form + {{そうです|sō desu}}.** To pass on something you heard or read, add {{そうです|sō desu}} to the plain form: {{結婚するそうです|kekkon suru sō desu}} “I hear he's getting married”. Nouns and な-adjectives take {{だ|da}}: {{雨だそうです|ame da sō desu}} “I hear it'll rain”. To say where it comes from: {{ニュースによると|nyūsu ni yoru to}} “according to the news”.

**Not the same {{そう|sō}}!** Compare the last lesson: {{おいしそうです|oishisō desu}} (without the {{い|i}}) “it looks delicious”, but {{おいしいそうです|oishii sō desu}} (the full plain form) “I hear it's delicious”.

table: {{雨が降りそうです。|Ame ga furisō desu.}}
{{雨が降るそうです。|Ame ga furu sō desu.}}
I hear it's going to rain.
{{おいしいそうです。|Oishii sō desu.}}

blocks.p: **Casual: {{って|tte}}.** With friends, put {{って|tte}} after the plain form: {{田中さん、結婚するって|Tanaka-san, kekkon suru tte}} “Tanaka's getting married, he says”. {{って|tte}} is the casual {{と|to}} for quoting.

**Apparently: {{らしいです|rashii desu}}.** For something you've gathered but can't quite confirm: {{あの店はおいしいらしいです|ano mise wa oishii rashii desu}} “Apparently that place is good”. Nouns and な-adjectives go straight before it: {{友達らしいです|tomodachi rashii desu}}.

ex.t: 天気予報によると、明日は雪だそうです。
ex.r: Tenki yohō ni yoru to, ashita wa yuki da sō desu.
ex.tr: According to the weather forecast, it's going to snow tomorrow.

ex.t: 新しいカフェはおいしいらしいですよ。
ex.r: Atarashii kafe wa oishii rashii desu yo.
ex.tr: Apparently the new café is good.

ex.t: ゆいさんは風邪で休むって。
ex.r: Yui-san wa kaze de yasumu tte.
ex.tr: Yui says she's off sick with a cold.

ex.t: 先生は昔、アメリカに住んでいたそうです。
ex.r: Sensei wa mukashi, Amerika ni sunde ita sō desu.
ex.tr: I hear our teacher used to live in America.

ex.t: このお寺は八百年前からあるそうです。
ex.r: Kono otera wa happyaku-nen mae kara aru sō desu.
ex.tr: Apparently this temple has been here for eight hundred years.

ex.t: 田中さんは来ないそうです。
ex.r: Tanaka-san wa konai sō desu.
ex.tr: I hear Mr Tanaka isn't coming.

blocks.tip: Office news often starts with {{聞きましたか|kikimashita ka}} “Have you heard?” and ends with {{そうですよ|sō desu yo}}.

mistakes.rr: Ashita wa ame da sō desu.
mistakes.why: To report news about a noun, add {{だ|da}}: {{雨だそうです|ame da sō desu}}.

mistakes.wrong: あの店はおいしそうです。
mistakes.right: あの店はおいしいそうです。
mistakes.rr: Ano mise wa oishii sō desu.
mistakes.tr: I hear that place is good.
mistakes.why: “I hear” uses the full plain form: {{おいしい|oishii}} + {{そうです|sō desu}}. {{おいしそう|oishisō}} means “it looks delicious”.

practice.q: Choose the missing word.
practice.t: 明日は雪だ___です。
practice.tr: I hear it'll snow tomorrow.
practice.why: Noun + {{だ|da}} + {{そうです|sō desu}}: “I hear”.

practice.q: {{田中さんは来ないそうです。|Tanaka-san wa konai sō desu.}} means…
options: I hear Mr Tanaka isn't coming.
Mr Tanaka looks like he isn't coming.
practice.why: Full plain form + {{そうです|sō desu}}: news you heard.

practice.q: Which one means “I hear it's delicious”?
options: {{おいしいそうです。|Oishii sō desu.}}
practice.why: Keep the {{い|i}} for “I hear”.

practice.q: A friend has news. Choose your replies.

lines.t: ねえ、聞いた？ケンが会社をやめるって。
lines.r: Nē, kiita? Ken ga kaisha o yameru tte.
lines.tr: Hey, did you hear? Ken says he's quitting his job.

options: え、本当？どうしてやめるの？

lessons.title: Say what you're thinking of doing
lessons.summary: Suggest things casually, and talk about plans you're considering: “Let's eat something!” “I'm thinking of studying in Japan.”
lessons.topic: the volitional form: {{行こう|ikō}}, {{食べよう|tabeyō}}; {{～ようと思っています|… yō to omotte imasu}}

goal.t: 来年、日本に留学しようと思っています。
goal.r: Rainen, Nihon ni ryūgaku shiyō to omotte imasu.
goal.tr: I'm thinking of studying in Japan next year.

dialog.t: お腹すいた。何か食べよう。
dialog.r: Onaka suita. Nanika tabeyō.
dialog.tr: I'm starving. Let's eat something.

dialog.t: うん、ラーメンにしよう。
dialog.r: Un, rāmen ni shiyō.
dialog.tr: Yeah, let's have ramen.

dialog.t: そういえば、夏休みは何をするの？
dialog.r: Sō ieba, natsuyasumi wa nani o suru no?
dialog.tr: By the way, what are you doing in the summer holidays?

dialog.t: アルバイトをしようと思ってる。秋に旅行したいから。
dialog.r: Arubaito o shiyō to omotteru. Aki ni ryokō shitai kara.
dialog.tr: I'm thinking of getting a part-time job. I want to travel in the autumn.

blocks.means: the form of a verb that means “let's…” or “I'll…”: {{行こう|ikō}} “let's go”.

blocks.p: **Let's (casual): the volitional form.** The plain version of {{ましょう|mashō}}. Group 1: the final u-sound becomes “ō”: {{行く|iku}} → {{行こう|ikō}}, {{飲む|nomu}} → {{飲もう|nomō}}, {{帰る|kaeru}} → {{帰ろう|kaerō}}. Group 2: {{る|ru}} → {{よう|yō}}: {{食べよう|tabeyō}}, {{見よう|miyō}}. Group 3: {{しよう|shiyō}}, {{来よう|koyō}}.

**I'm thinking of…: volitional + {{と思っています|to omotte imasu}}.** {{留学しようと思っています|ryūgaku shiyō to omotte imasu}} “I'm thinking of studying abroad”. It's softer and less fixed than {{つもり|tsumori}}: a plan you're still turning over. {{と思います|to omoimasu}} alone is for a decision made right now: {{今日は早く寝ようと思います|kyō wa hayaku neyō to omoimasu}} “I think I'll go to bed early tonight”. With friends: {{と思ってる|to omotteru}}.

ex.t: 疲れたね。ちょっと休もう。
ex.r: Tsukareta ne. Chotto yasumō.
ex.tr: We're tired, huh. Let's take a break.

ex.t: 一緒に帰ろう。
ex.r: Issho ni kaerō.

ex.t: 週末は家の掃除をしようと思っています。

ex.t: 仕事を変えようと思っています。

ex.tr: I'm thinking of changing jobs.

ex.t: 今日は早く寝ようと思います。
ex.r: Kyō wa hayaku neyō to omoimasu.
ex.tr: I think I'll go to bed early tonight.

ex.r: Yoshi, ganbarō!
ex.tr: Right, let's do this!

blocks.tip: {{がんばろう！|ganbarō!}} “Let's do our best!” and {{がんばって！|ganbatte!}} “Good luck, go for it!” are two of the most-used phrases in Japanese.

lessons.title: Say what happened to you
lessons.summary: Tell about things done to you, good or bad: “My wallet was stolen.” “My teacher praised me.” “I got caught in the rain.”
lessons.topic: the passive: {{盗まれました|nusumaremashita}}, {{ほめられました|homeraremashita}}, {{雨に降られました|ame ni furaremashita}}

goal.t: 電車で財布を盗まれました。
goal.r: Densha de saifu o nusumaremashita.
goal.tr: My wallet was stolen on the train.

dialog.t: どうしましたか。
dialog.r: Dō shimashita ka.
dialog.tr: What's happened?

dialog.t: 電車の中で財布を盗まれたんです。
dialog.r: Densha no naka de saifu o nusumareta n desu.
dialog.tr: My wallet was stolen on the train.

dialog.t: それは大変でしたね。何が入っていましたか。
dialog.r: Sore wa taihen deshita ne. Nani ga haitte imashita ka.
dialog.tr: That's terrible. What was in it?

dialog.t: お金とカードです。それに、帰りに雨に降られて、びしょぬれです…。
dialog.r: Okane to kādo desu. Sore ni, kaeri ni ame ni furarete, bishonure desu…
dialog.tr: Money and cards. And on top of that, I got caught in the rain on the way, and I'm soaked…

dialog.t: じゃ、まずこの紙に名前と住所を書いてください。
dialog.r: Ja, mazu kono kami ni namae to jūsho o kaite kudasai.
dialog.tr: Right. First, please write your name and address on this form.

blocks.means: a form of the verb that tells what was done to someone: “was stolen”, “was praised”.

blocks.p: **Something done to you: the passive.** Group 1: the final u-sound becomes an a-sound + {{れる|reru}}: {{盗む|nusumu}} “steal” → {{盗まれる|nusumareru}} “be stolen”, {{言う|iu}} → {{言われる|iwareru}} “be told”. Group 2: {{る|ru}} → {{られる|rareru}}: {{ほめる|homeru}} → {{ほめられる|homerareru}} “be praised”. Group 3: {{される|sareru}}, {{来られる|korareru}}. The passive is itself a group 2 verb: {{盗まれました|nusumaremashita}}.

**The doer takes {{に|ni}}:** {{先生にほめられました|sensei ni homeraremashita}} “I was praised by my teacher”. What was taken keeps {{を|o}}: {{財布を盗まれました|saifu o nusumaremashita}}, word for word “I was wallet-stolen”. The person it happened to is the topic, and is often left out.

**The suffering passive.** Japanese also uses the passive for things not done to anyone, to say they affected you badly: {{雨に降られました|ame ni furaremashita}} “I got rained on”, {{隣の人にたばこを吸われました|tonari no hito ni tabako o suwaremashita}} “the person next to me smoked (and I had to put up with it)”.

**News and signs** use the passive a lot, as English does: {{このお寺は八百年前に建てられました|kono otera wa happyaku-nen mae ni tateraremashita}} “This temple was built 800 years ago”. Notice that group 2 passives look exactly like the potential ({{食べられる|taberareru}} is “can eat” or “be eaten”): the sentence tells you which.

ex.t: 先生にほめられました。
ex.r: Sensei ni homeraremashita.
ex.tr: My teacher praised me.

ex.t: 帰りに雨に降られました。
ex.r: Kaeri ni ame ni furaremashita.
ex.tr: I got caught in the rain on the way home.

ex.t: 母にしかられました。
ex.r: Haha ni shikararemashita.
ex.tr: I got told off by my mother.

ex.t: 電車で足を踏まれました。
ex.r: Densha de ashi o fumaremashita.
ex.tr: Someone stepped on my foot on the train.

ex.t: このお寺は八百年前に建てられました。
ex.r: Kono otera wa happyaku-nen mae ni tateraremashita.
ex.tr: This temple was built eight hundred years ago.

ex.t: よく若く見えると言われます。
ex.r: Yoku wakaku mieru to iwaremasu.
ex.tr: People often tell me I look young.

blocks.tip: {{言われます|iwaremasu}} “I'm told” is handy for passing on what people say about you: {{よく母に似ていると言われます|yoku haha ni nite iru to iwaremasu}} “People often say I look like my mother”.

lessons.title: Understand polite Japanese in shops and offices
lessons.summary: Recognise the special polite words that staff and officials use, and use a few yourself: “Please wait a moment.” “My name is Smith.”
lessons.topic: keigo: respectful words ({{いらっしゃる|irassharu}}, {{召し上がる|meshiagaru}}), humble words ({{申す|mōsu}}, {{いただく|itadaku}}), {{お～ください|o … kudasai}}, {{でございます|de gozaimasu}}

goal.t: 少々お待ちください。
goal.r: Shōshō omachi kudasai.
goal.tr: Please wait a moment.

dialog.t: いらっしゃいませ。ご予約のお名前をお願いいたします。
dialog.r: Irasshaimase. Go-yoyaku no onamae o onegai itashimasu.
dialog.tr: Welcome. May I have the name on your reservation?

dialog.t: スミスです。
dialog.r: Sumisu desu.
dialog.tr: Smith.

dialog.t: スミス様でございますね。少々お待ちください。…お待たせいたしました。お部屋は八階でございます。
dialog.r: Sumisu-sama de gozaimasu ne. Shōshō omachi kudasai. … Omatase itashimashita. Oheya wa hachi-kai de gozaimasu.
dialog.tr: Mr Smith, yes. Please wait a moment. …Thank you for waiting. Your room is on the eighth floor.

dialog.t: 朝ご飯は何時からですか。
dialog.r: Asagohan wa nan-ji kara desu ka.
dialog.tr: What time is breakfast?

dialog.t: 七時から、二階のレストランでございます。ごゆっくりどうぞ。
dialog.r: Shichi-ji kara, ni-kai no resutoran de gozaimasu. Goyukkuri dōzo.
dialog.tr: From seven, in the restaurant on the second floor. Enjoy your stay.

blocks.means: “respect language”: special polite words and forms used to customers, superiors and strangers.

blocks.p: **Keigo.** In shops, hotels, offices and announcements you'll hear **keigo**, words and forms that raise the customer or lower the speaker. As a learner you don't need to produce much of it (polite です/ます is fine), but you do need to understand it.

**Respectful words raise the other person**, for what *they* do, never for yourself: {{いらっしゃいます|irasshaimasu}} go, come, be; {{召し上がります|meshiagarimasu}} eat, drink; {{なさいます|nasaimasu}} do; {{おっしゃいます|osshaimasu}} say; {{ご覧になります|goran ni narimasu}} look. And a pattern for requests: {{お～ください|o … kudasai}}: {{お待ちください|omachi kudasai}} “please wait”, {{お入りください|ohairi kudasai}} “please come in”.

**Humble words lower the speaker**, for what *I* do: {{申します|mōshimasu}} say, be called; {{いたします|itashimasu}} do; {{参ります|mairimasu}} go, come; {{いただきます|itadakimasu}} receive, eat. And {{でございます|de gozaimasu}} is an extra-polite {{です|desu}}.

**What you can use yourself, starting now:** {{～と申します|… to mōshimasu}} to give your name formally ({{スミスと申します|Sumisu to mōshimasu}}), {{いただきます|itadakimasu}} before eating, and {{お願いいたします|onegai itashimasu}} as an extra-polite “please”.

ex.tr: Thank you for waiting. (Sorry to keep you.)

blocks.tip: Station announcements are full of keigo: {{まもなく電車が参ります|mamonaku densha ga mairimasu}} “The train will arrive shortly”, {{白線の内側までお下がりください|hakusen no uchigawa made osagari kudasai}} “Please stand behind the white line”.

lessons.title: Tell a story, and what went wrong
lessons.summary: Put it all together to tell a story in order, with feelings and regrets: “I left my umbrella on the train!”
lessons.topic: {{～てしまいました|… te shimaimashita}}; telling a story with the past, the て-form, {{とき|toki}}, {{たら|tara}} and {{から|kara}}

goal.t: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました！
goal.r: Densha ni kasa o wasurete shimaimashita!
goal.tr: I left my umbrella on the train!

dialog.t: 週末の旅行はどうでしたか。

dialog.tr: Oh, poor you.

dialog.t: でも、夜はおいしい湯豆腐を食べて、元気になりました！
dialog.r: Demo, yoru wa oishii yudōfu o tabete, genki ni narimashita!
dialog.tr: But in the evening I had delicious tofu hot pot and cheered up!

blocks.p: **Something regrettable, or completely done: て-form + {{しまいました|shimaimashita}}.** {{忘れてしまいました|wasurete shimaimashita}} “I (went and) forgot”: it adds the feeling that it's done and can't be undone, usually with regret. It also means “finish completely”: {{全部食べてしまいました|zenbu tabete shimaimashita}} “I ate the whole thing”. With friends: {{～ちゃった|… chatta}} or {{～じゃった|… jatta}}: {{忘れちゃった|wasurechatta}}, {{飲んじゃった|nonjatta}}.

table: {{財布をなくしてしまいました。|Saifu o nakushite shimaimashita.}}
{{財布をなくしちゃった。|Saifu o nakushichatta.}}
I've gone and lost my wallet.
{{宿題を全部してしまいました。|Shukudai o zenbu shite shimaimashita.}}

blocks.p: **Telling a story.** You now have all the tools. Set the scene with {{とき|toki}} ({{京都に着いたとき|Kyōto ni tsuita toki}}), or with {{たら|tara}} for what you found ({{着いたら、雨が降っていて|tsuitara, ame ga futte ite}} “when I arrived, it was raining”). Link events with the て-form, give reasons with {{から|kara}} and {{ので|node}}, describe what was going on with {{ていました|te imashita}}, say how you felt with past adjectives, and use {{てしまいました|te shimaimashita}} for what went wrong. Story words: {{それで|sorede}} “so”, {{それから|sorekara}} “after that”, {{でも|demo}} “but”, {{結局|kekkyoku}} “in the end”.

**Keep it alive.** Storytellers explain with {{んです|n desu}}: {{寝坊したんです|nebō shita n desu}} “I overslept, you see”. Listeners react: {{え|e}} “what?”, {{それで？|sorede?}} “and then?”, {{かわいそうに|kawaisō ni}} “poor you”, {{よかったですね|yokatta desu ne}} “I'm glad”.

ex.t: ケーキを全部食べてしまいました。
ex.r: Kēki o zenbu tabete shimaimashita.
ex.tr: I ate the whole cake.

ex.t: 寝坊して、会議に遅れてしまいました。
ex.r: Nebō shite, kaigi ni okurete shimaimashita.
ex.tr: I overslept and was late for the meeting.

ex.t: 京都に着いたら、雨が降っていました。
ex.r: Kyōto ni tsuitara, ame ga futte imashita.
ex.tr: When I arrived in Kyoto, it was raining.

ex.t: 道に迷ったとき、親切な人が駅まで連れていってくれました。
ex.r: Michi ni mayotta toki, shinsetsu na hito ga eki made tsurete itte kuremashita.
ex.tr: When I got lost, a kind person took me to the station.

ex.t: 結局、とても楽しい旅行になりました。
ex.r: Kekkyoku, totemo tanoshii ryokō ni narimashita.
ex.tr: In the end, it turned into a really fun trip.

ex.t: スマホを落としちゃった。
ex.r: Sumaho o otoshichatta.
ex.tr: I've gone and dropped my phone.

blocks.tip: A Japanese story often ends with how you feel about it now: {{いい思い出になりました|ii omoide ni narimashita}} “It became a good memory”.

mistakes.wrong: 傘を忘れりしまいました。
mistakes.right: 傘を忘れてしまいました。
mistakes.why: {{しまう|shimau}} follows the て-form: {{忘れて|wasurete}}.

mistakes.wrong: ビールを全部飲みちゃった。
mistakes.right: ビールを全部飲んじゃった。
mistakes.why: The casual {{ちゃった|chatta}} / {{じゃった|jatta}} comes from the て-form: {{飲んで|nonde}} → {{飲んじゃった|nonjatta}}.

practice.q: Choose the missing ending.
practice.t: 電車にかばんを忘れ___しまいました。
practice.r: Densha ni kaban o wasure___ shimaimashita.
practice.tr: I left my bag on the train.
practice.why: て-form + {{しまいました|shimaimashita}}.

practice.q: {{ケーキを全部食べてしまいました。|Kēki o zenbu tabete shimaimashita.}} means…
options: I'm going to eat the whole cake.
practice.why: {{てしまいました|te shimaimashita}}: completely done, with a hint of regret.

practice.q: Choose the missing ending.
practice.t: 京都に着い___、雨が降っていました。
practice.r: Kyōto ni tsui___, ame ga futte imashita.
practice.tr: When I arrived in Kyoto, it was raining.
practice.why: What you found when you arrived: {{着いたら|tsuitara}}.

practice.q: A friend tells you a story. React!

lines.t: 昨日、スマホを落としちゃった。
lines.r: Kinō, sumaho o otoshichatta.
lines.tr: I dropped my phone yesterday.

lines.why: Ask for the rest of the story: {{それで？|sorede?}} “and then?”.

lines.t: でも、駅員さんが見つけてくれたんだ。
lines.r: Demo, ekiin-san ga mitsukete kureta n da.
lines.tr: But a station attendant found it for me.

lines.why: Good news: {{よかったね|yokatta ne}}.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.tr: I overslept and was late for the meeting.
practice.why: {{寝坊して、会議に遅れてしまいました。|Nebō shite, kaigi ni okurete shimaimashita.}}

practice.q: Tell a friend: “My bike got stolen!” (casually)
practice.answer: 自転車を盗まれちゃった！

practice.q: Your turn: tell a short story about a trip or a day when something went wrong. Use the past, the て-form, {{とき|toki}} or {{たら|tara}}, and {{てしまいました|te shimaimashita}}.

answers.t: 去年、大阪へ行ったとき、駅で財布をなくしてしまいました。でも、親切な人が交番に届けてくれたので、本当に助かりました。
answers.r: Kyonen, Ōsaka e itta toki, eki de saifu o nakushite shimaimashita. Demo, shinsetsu na hito ga kōban ni todokete kureta node, hontō ni tasukarimashita.
answers.tr: Last year, when I went to Osaka, I lost my wallet at the station. But a kind person took it to the police box, so I was really lucky.

answers.t: 先週、友達の誕生日を忘れてしまいました。次の日、ケーキを持っていって、謝りました。友達は笑って、許してくれました。
answers.r: Senshū, tomodachi no tanjōbi o wasurete shimaimashita. Tsugi no hi, kēki o motte itte, ayamarimashita. Tomodachi wa waratte, yurushite kuremashita.
answers.tr: Last week I forgot a friend's birthday. The next day I took a cake round and apologised. My friend laughed and forgave me.
